assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Ideal fluid
items.clue: Model liquid or gas that cannot be compressed and has no internal friction.

items.label: Bernoulli's equation
items.clue: Energy conservation per unit volume for a flow, linking P, height y and speed v.

items.label: Equilibrium position
items.clue: Place where an oscillating object would rest; the restoring force is zero there.

items.label: Pendulum
items.clue: Its period is longer with a longer string and is unchanged by the mass of the bob.

questions.stem: The density of aluminium is 2.7 g cm⁻³. What is the volume, in m³, of an aluminium block of mass 0.081 kg?
Honey poured from a jar flows much more slowly than water. A student models the honey as an ideal fluid. Which property of real honey does this model leave out?

options.text: Its resistance to flowing, which slows layers of honey that slide past one another.
Its large density, which is the property that makes honey thick and slow to pour.
Its ability to change shape, which an incompressible fluid does not have.
Its liquid state, since the ideal-fluid model applies only to gases.

questions.stem: A pendulum bob swings to and fro in a small arc. At the lowest point of its swing, what are its acceleration along its path and its speed?

options.text: Acceleration along the path greatest; speed zero.
Acceleration along the path zero; speed greatest.
Acceleration along the path zero; speed also zero.
Acceleration along the path greatest; speed greatest.

questions.explanation: The lowest point is equilibrium: the restoring force along the path is zero there. The bob sped up all the way down and starts to slow on the way up, so its speed is greatest here.

questions.stem: A block attached to an ideal spring oscillates on a horizontal surface with negligible friction, with period T. The block is replaced by a block with 4 times the mass, and the new block is set oscillating with 3 times the original amplitude. The new period is how many times T?

A block of mass m attached to an ideal spring of spring constant k oscillates with amplitude A on a horizontal surface with negligible friction. Which expression gives the speed of the block when it is at x = A/2, halfway between the equilibrium position and a turning point?
A block of ice keeps its own shape, but the water it melts into takes the shape of whatever holds it. Which explanation, in terms of the water molecules, accounts for this difference?

options.text: The molecules in the ice are themselves hard and rigid, while the molecules in liquid water are soft and able to change their shape.
In the ice the molecules are packed tightly together; in the liquid they are several times farther apart, so they are free to move.
The molecules in the ice do not move at all, while the molecules in the liquid are constantly moving around one another.
Interactions keep each molecule near one place in the ice; in the liquid, molecules stay close but can move past each other.

questions.stem: Water flows steadily through a completely filled horizontal pipe. In a wide section, where the pressure is P₁, the cross-sectional area is A₁ and the water's speed is v. The pipe then narrows to a section of area A₁/2, where the pressure is P₂. Treat the water as an ideal fluid of density ρ. Which expression gives P₁ − P₂?

A block attached to a horizontal ideal spring oscillates on a surface with negligible friction. At an instant when the block's kinetic energy has its minimum value, which of the following is true of the spring potential energy U_s of the block–spring system?

options.text: It is zero, because the block is momentarily at rest.
It has its maximum value, equal to the system's total energy.
It has its minimum value, as the system then has the least energy.
It has the same value as at every other instant of the motion.

questions.stem: Water leaves the end of hose 1 with speed v. Hose 2 has half the inner diameter of hose 1, and water leaves its end with speed 2v. Both hoses are completely filled, and the water can be treated as an ideal fluid. The volume of water leaving hose 2 each second is what multiple of the volume leaving hose 1 each second?

options.text: ×½
